answer: Private defence can apply in situations where a person is attempting to prevent theft, as outlined in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. According to Section 35, individuals have the right to defend their own body and the body of others against offences affecting the human body, as well as to protect property against theft. Furthermore, Section 41 specifies that the right of private defence extends to causing harm to the wrong-doer if the act of theft creates a reasonable apprehension of death or grievous hurt. Therefore, if your actions were in response to a theft and you had a reasonable belief that you needed to act to prevent harm, private defence may be applicable.
summary_answer: Yes, private defence can apply if you injured someone while trying to stop a theft, provided the circumstances justified the use of force.
